subject: Ingress fabric selection for private deployment
messages:
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme-analytics.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: SRE Team <sre@acme-analytics.com>, Lara Singh <lara.singh@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment connectivity options — quick run-through

Kimberly,

Thanks for taking the call earlier. As we start scoping the private deployment (VPC + dedicated inference nodes) for Acme Analytics, our security team asked for a concise comparison between three candidate ingress patterns: VPC Peering, PrivateLink (interface endpoints), and Site-to-Site VPN. Key constraints:

- Sensitive PII workloads (SOC 2 and internal encryption-at-rest/in-transit requirements)
- Cross-account isolation (we'd like minimal blast radius)
- Multiregion (primary us-west-2, DR in us-east-1)
- Throughput: bursts up to ~2Gbps sustained for short windows

Can you share a short matrix with security tradeoffs, operational complexity, and any hard limits (throughput, cross-region support)? Also curious about failover patterns and recommended pilot configuration.

If useful, I can loop in our NetOps lead.

Thanks,
Tom Reynolds
Enterprise Architect — Acme Analytics

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: SRE Team <sre@acme-analytics.com>, Lara Singh <lara.singh@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment connectivity options — quick run-through

Tom — thanks, this is perfect context. Attached is a compact matrix (network-options-matrix.xlsx) that maps the three patterns to security posture, latency/throughput characteristics, operational runbook items, and cost signals. High-level summary below.

High-level tradeoffs (short):
- VPC Peering: Low latency, seamless IP-level connectivity, good for high-throughput; cross-account peering can be managed but adds routing/ACL complexity. No native cross-region peering in some clouds (or it costs more). Lacks an explicit proxy boundary, so workload isolation depends on routing + security groups.
- PrivateLink (interface endpoints): Strong isolation (explicit endpoint + endpoint service), better for strict data exfiltration controls and compliance. Easier to limit access to specific services. Throughput per ENI/IPsec-like overhead can be a limiting factor — recommend testing at target bursts. Usually simpler to audit.
- Site-to-Site VPN: Fast to stand up and familiar to many infra teams. Good as a fallback path. Can add encryption boundaries, but tunnels are generally higher latency and harder to operate for bursty high-throughput workloads; requires NAT and careful MTU tuning.

Recommended pilot: PrivateLink in us-west-2 with a paired S2S VPN to test failover/operational play. If throughput spike testing shows issues, consider peering for the compute-heavy path and use PrivateLink for control plane + metadata and sensitive routes.

Attachments: network-options-matrix.xlsx (summary + suggested test plan)

Next steps: 1) Can you confirm SRE availability to run a 2-hour throughput + failover test? 2) Any procurement/security blockers for creating an endpoint service?

—

Kimberly — thanks for the matrix. A couple of follow-ups from our security team after a quick read: 

1) For PrivateLink, do you have guidance on how audit logs and flow visibility are surfaced to the customer (we need proof of egress/ingress for SOC 2 evidence)?
2) If we choose a mixed approach (peering + PrivateLink), how do you recommend handling routing priorities and split-horizon DNS so control plane calls prefer PrivateLink while bulk inference traffic prefers peering?
3) For S2S VPN as fallback: what are common MTU/fragmentation issues you’ve seen with LLM inference payloads? Our payloads include long JSON-based requests and sometimes base64 attachments.

We're able to schedule a 2-hour SRE window next Tue but want to lock the specific test cases.

Thanks,
Tom

Tom / Kimberly — quick note from the infra perspective. We've done this pattern several times with regulated customers. My recommendation:

- Default to PrivateLink for control-plane and any flows that require strict tenant isolation/auditability. PrivateLink gives a clean service boundary and easier KMS/HSM integration because traffic never traverses a public gateway.
- For heavy token generation paths where you need predictable throughput and low latency, prefer VPC Peering (or cross-account Transit) inside the same region. Peering avoids ENI bottlenecks and is simpler for large payloads.
- Use S2S VPN as a soft-fallback (DR/failover). Keep it as a monitored, throttled path — don’t make it the primary for heavy traffic.

Operational notes:
- PrivateLink: test ENI scaling in your target AZs; some clouds limit endpoints per AZ or per ENI. Document the audit log collection (flow logs + endpoint service logs) as part of the SOC 2 pack.
- Peering: ensure route table hygiene and guardrails (no broad 0.0.0.0/0 leaking).
- VPN: tune MTU to 1400-1420 (depends on encryption headers) and test for fragmentation on your large JSON payloads.

I’m attaching a short checklist (privatelink-s2s-checklist.pdf) that our onboarding team uses. Happy to run the SRE test plan with Acme next Tue if you confirm the window.

—
Ben Carter
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Private deployment connectivity options — quick run-through

Tom — quick synthesis and proposed decision path so we can move to scheduling and procurement: 

1) Pilot: PrivateLink-only pilot for control plane and small-volume inference baseline in us-west-2. Validate audit log collection, endpoint throughput (target 2Gbps bursts), and ENI scaling. Run two 1-hour load windows.
2) Parallel throughput test: create a peered VPC in the same region (peering/transit) and run a heavy-path test to confirm latency and sustained throughput—this will be our plan B if PrivateLink cannot meet burst requirements.
3) Fallback: Configure S2S VPN between Acme on-prem and the VPC for DR failover testing (exercise route priorities and MTU).
4) Deliverables: test report with metrics (p95 latency, sustained throughput, packet loss, MTU/fragments) + SOC 2 evidence checklist.

Action items: Kimberly / Ben to staff SRE test windows next Tue (please confirm time). Tom / Lara to confirm NetOps contact and any procurement approvals needed to create endpoint services. Jonas — tagging you for any notes about cross-region DR (we'll keep DR out of scope for the first pilot).

Thanks — aiming to have the pilot scheduled by next Wed and test artifacts delivered within one week of the run.

Best,
